endorsements.label: How Unique Is Your Browser?
endorsements.description: This talk reports the results of the panopticlick browser fingerprinting experiment. We show how inoccent-looking version and configuration information can be used to uniquely identify almost all desktop browsers, without use of cookies or IP addresses. We discuss how this comes about, how serious a problem it is, and just how hard it will be to fix...

endorsements.name: Peter Eckersley
endorsements.label: Let's Encrypt - Minting Free Certificates to Encrypt the Entire Web
endorsements.description: Let's Encrypt is a new certificate authority that is being launched by EFF in collaboration with Mozilla, Cisco, Akamai, IdenTrust, and a team at the University of Michigan. It will issue certificates for free, using a new automated protocol called ACME for verification of domain control and issuance. This talk will describe the features of the CA and available clients at launch; explore the security challenges inherent in building such a system; and its effect on the security of the CA marketplace as a whole. We will also update our place on the roadmap to a Web that uses HTTPS by default.
